what_it_is_best_for: Answering routine calls and messages when safe scripts and human handoff rules are clear
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Call categories, allowed admin replies, escalation owner, transcript QA sample, downtime path
red_flags_to_pause: Vendor implies clinical triage, diagnosis, emergency handling, guaranteed booking growth or GDPR compliance
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=no handoff evidence; 3=basic scripts and escalation; 5=audited stop rules and owner review
aics_fit_boundary: AICS can map safe handoff evidence before deployment but does not provide clinical or legal approval

what_it_is_best_for: Managing appointments records reminders billing modules and existing clinic workflow
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Current PMS gaps, integration list, user ownership, export limits, reminder consent evidence
red_flags_to_pause: Buyer treats PMS purchase as proof that missed-call leakage or consent questions are solved
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=no owner or process evidence; 3=known gap list; 5=workflow owner and integration limits documented
aics_fit_boundary: AICS can produce an owner decision memo before switching or extending PMS modules

what_it_is_best_for: Structured reminders recalls campaigns and patient communications where consent and templates are owned
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Message types, consent basis questions, template approvals, opt-out path, staff owner
red_flags_to_pause: Platform is used to send broad messages without DPO/privacy review or stop rules
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=no consent/template owner; 3=some template governance; 5=reviewed message categories and exception handling
aics_fit_boundary: AICS can organise evidence questions but does not certify GDPR or clinical appropriateness

what_it_is_best_for: Human coverage for peak hours after-hours and admin overflow
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Call reason taxonomy, service scripts, escalation SLA, redacted sample log, complaints path
red_flags_to_pause: Service captures sensitive data without boundary rules or qualified escalation
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=no script/escalation proof; 3=basic call log; 5=owner-reviewed categories and redaction rules
aics_fit_boundary: AICS can design no-patient-data evaluation criteria before vendor onboarding

what_it_is_best_for: Discovery and appointment demand through a third-party marketplace
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Listing accuracy, cancellation policy, source attribution, conversion ownership, review management boundary
red_flags_to_pause: Marketplace traffic is mistaken for owned patient relationship or guaranteed acquisition
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=no attribution; 3=listing and attribution known; 5=source-to-owner map with leakage review
aics_fit_boundary: AICS can map source leakage and owner follow-up but does not claim demand or rankings

what_it_is_best_for: Campaign traffic generation when conversion and follow-up evidence already exists
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Landing page evidence, response SLA, call/form routing, consent wording, campaign claim review
red_flags_to_pause: More spend is approved before missed calls forms and owner queues are measured
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=no conversion evidence; 3=basic tracking; 5=lead source and response ownership documented
aics_fit_boundary: AICS can review readiness before ad spend without claiming patient growth or ROI

what_it_is_best_for: No-credentials review before platform adviser agency or automation spend
evidence_to_request_before_spend: Redacted screenshots, synthetic sample rows, owner interviews, policy pointers, missing-evidence log
red_flags_to_pause: Buyer expects implementation guarantees compliance sign-off or patient/revenue outcomes from a diagnostic
score_0_to_5_guidance: 0=insufficient owner access; 3=basic evidence pack; 5=clear no-credentials scope and stop rules
aics_fit_boundary: AICS fit is evidence organisation and safe next-step selection; not legal clinical GDPR CQC DTAC DSPT or ROI proof
